title: mapStructuralOp swaps the `>` direct-child and `>>` descendant relations
notes:
mapStructuralOp (internal/traceql/lower.go) is the exact seam Tempo's OpSpansetChild / OpSpansetDescendant enum maps to chplan.StructuralChild / chplan.StructuralDescendant; this patch swaps the two return values, so `>` lowers to descendant-reachability and `>>` lowers to direct-child-only. Both detectors seed the SAME bounded branching-tree fixture #3444/#3518 added to gen/traceql.go (root -> childA -> grandchild, root -> childB) so the depth-two case is a real, wire-observed discriminator rather than an assumed one: the direct-child query `{root} > {grandchild}` must return zero matches and the descendant query `{root} >> {grandchild}` must return exactly one, on both the HTTP /api/search transport (test/property/traceql_test.go, real parse->lower->optimize->emit->chDB->HTTP pipeline) and the gRPC streaming Search RPC (internal/api/tempo/grpc, real *grpc.Server over bufconn against the same chDB session) independently. Both were hand-verified to fail (kill) against this exact patch and to pass cleanly against the unmutated tree before this record was added.

Limits: the branching-tree fixture is a single FIXED topology (branching factor 2, max depth 2 — traceQLBranchingTreeSpanCount in gen/traceql.go) and only chdb-backed local pipelines are exercised here — no live reference-Tempo differential (compatibility/tempo/driver) carries an equivalent grandchild-depth structural case today; its seeder fixture is a flat root+children shape with no third generation, so `>` and `>>` never diverge there. See issue #3528 for a related, separately-filed contracts.json documentation gap this same generator strengthening exposed.
